newsitem.title: USA: Agouron to start trials of anticancer agent.
newsitem.headline: Agouron to start trials of anticancer agent.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday it received Food and Drug Administration clearance to begin clinical studies in the U.S. of its anti-cancer agent, AG3340.

The company said in a statement it will start by conducting extended, dose-escalation studies in patients with advanced cancer. It plans to follow with longer term clinical trials with its partner, Roche Holding Ltd's Hoffman La-Roche.
Agouron earlier this year reported results of a Phase I trial in Edinburgh, Scotland, which showed AG3340 was well tolerated and rapidly absorbed, the company said.

AG3340 is a small, synthetic molecule designed to selectively inactivate certain enzymes believed to play a key role in the growth and metastasis of many malignant tumors. Since related enzymes are believed to be involved in normal adult biological processes, the compound's ability to selectively target enzymes is critical.
